topics.title: Parts of the Mouth | Materials used for Caring for the Mouth Primary 3 (Basic 3) - Home Economics
topics.content:
HOME ECONOMICS
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
THIRD TERM
WEEK 2
PRIMARY 3
THEME - HEALTHY LIVING
PREVIOUS LESSON - Exam Questions - Second Term Examination Home Economics Primary 3 (Basic 3) Link
TOPIC - CARE OF THE MOUTH AND TOOTH
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2.Parts of the Mouth
3. Materials used for Mouth Cleaning
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. mention the parts of the mouth.
2. list the materials used for cleaning the mouth.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify different parts of the mouth and materials used for caring for the mouth.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Toothbrushes
2. Tooth paste
3. Charcoal, salt
4. Chewing sticks
5. Cotton wool
6. Tooth polishing powder.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
WRITING INSTRUCTION
Copy as I write or draw as I write. This instruction should be given when you need the pupils to write or draw.
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s/Pupil’s Activities - Display chart showing different parts of the mouth for the pupils to identify and point to each parts of their mouth.
Pupil’s Activities - This is my mouth, teeth, tongue and gum.
Teacher’s remark - Correct. The parts of the mouth are lips, teeth, tongue and gum. Write the parts of the mouth on the board and ask the pupils to state materials used for caring for the mouth.
PARTS OF THE MOUTH
1. Lips
2. Teeth
3. Tongue
4. Gum
MODERN MOUTH CLEANING MATERIALS
1. Toothbrushes
2. Toothpaste
TRADITIONAL MOUTH CLEANING MATERIALS
1. Chewing sticks
2. Charcoal
3. Salt
4. Cotton wool or foam
5. Native polishing powder
LESSON 2 - HOW TO CARE FOR MOUTH (PRACTICAL)
Practical Demonstration on the use of modern and traditional cleaning articles.
ASSIGNMENT
Find out the dangers of not caring for the mouth.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Assembles articles for mouth cleaning.
Pupil’s Activities - Bring mouth and teeth cleaning materials to the class.
3. Demonstrates the correct way of cleaning the mouth and paying attention to the tongue.
Pupil’s Activities - Practice the correct way of cleaning the mouth and paying attention to the tongue.
4. Demonstrates the use of traditional cleaning articles.
Pupil’s Activities - Practice the use of traditional teeth cleaning materials. Clean their teeth with chewing stick.
5. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Danger of not Caring for the Mouth | Dangers of sharing Toothbrush or Chewing sticks Primary 3 (Basic 3) - Home Economics
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask the pupils to:
1. mention three ways they keep the mouth clean.
2. name two traditional materials for keeping the mouth clean.

HOME ECONOMICS
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
THIRD TERM
WEEK
PRIMARY 3
THEME - HEALTHY LIVING
PREVIOUS LESSON -
TOPIC - PERSONAL HEALTH RULES
LEARNING AREA
1. Meaning of Personal Health Rules
2. Importance of Good Rest and Sleep
3. Importance of Good Posture
4. Effects of Rough Play
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. explain the rules for healthy living.
2. practice good health habits.
3. state roles of good health in development and growth.
4. explain the need for daily sleep and rest.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Care of the Body
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Chart of rules for healthy living.
2. First aid box.
3. Chart on correct posture e.g. sitting, bending, walking, etc.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
WRITING INSTRUCTION
Copy as I write or draw as I write. This instruction should be given when you need the pupils to write or draw.
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTORY QUESTIONS
Teacher’s/Pupil’s Activities - Asks the pupils to state the reasons why we must take care of our body.
Teacher’s Activities - Listen to the pupil’s discussions and relates to personal health. For example, taking care of our body means taking care of our personal health.
PERSONAL HEALTH RULES
Personal health rules are rules set to ensure personal hygiene or cleanliness. For example, taking your bath regularly, brushing your teeth twice a day, washing your hand after toilet, etc.
RULES FOR HEALTHY LIVING
1. Wash and clean various parts of the body
2. Wear clean clothes.
3. Maintain good health habits at home and at school.
4. Always clean your surroundings.
5. Drink only clean water.
6. Work hard and play well.
7. Regular exercise, etc.
GOOD HEALTH HABITS
Teacher’s/Pupil’s Activities - Practical Demonstration Personal Health Rules.
THE IMPORTANCE OF REST AND SLEEP
1. It promotes growth and development.
2. It boosts learning.
3. It reduces injury risk.
4. It improves attention and behaviour.
5. It prepares the body for another day.
6. It improves productivity.
7. It improves and increases the quality of life.
REASONS FOR GOOD POSTURE
1. It reduces stress in the body.
2. It helps blood circulation.
3. It increases energy levels.
4. It enhances lung capacity.
5. It aids digestion.
6. It boosts self confidence.
EFFECTS OF ROUGH PLAY
Rough play is different from normal play. It is hard, not all children have the strength.
Rough play includes - wrestle, climbing and playing on the tree or fence, climb over each other, pretend to fight, roll around, etc.
It has both positive and negative effects. Rough play also helps children gain self-control and become more emotionally confident. And also, leads to -
1. Real fight
2. Injuries (temporary or permanent)
3. Dislocation
4. Fracture
5. Internal bleeding
6. Death, if not controlled or managed.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Discusses health rules with pupils.
Pupil’s Activities - Discuss health rules with the teacher.
3. Relates rule to child’s home and school.
4. Discusses the advantages of good rest and sleep.
Pupil’s Activities - Practice sleeping and resting at appropriate times.
5. Integrate good health issues raised in class situation.
6. Discusses effects of rough play.
Pupil’s Activities - Contribute to discussion on what can happen during rough plays.
7. Discusses the importance of maintaining good posture.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate in the class discussion.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask the pupils to:
1. mention 5 rules.
2. name 3 types of accidents that can occur during play.
3. give 3 reasons why it is good to sleep or rest.
4. give 3 reasons why should maintain good posture.

HOME ECONOMICS

WEEK 7
PRIMARY 3

PREVIOUS LESSON - Nigerian Traditional Clothes | Wearing of Traditional Clothes Primary 3 (Basic 3) - Home Economics
TOPIC - BATHROOMS AND TOILETS
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Meaning and Types of Bathrooms and Toilets
3. Reasons for Cleaning the Bathrooms and Toilets
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. mention types of toilets and bathrooms.
2. explain the importance of taking good care of toilets and bathroom.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify and make use of bathrooms and toilets properly.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Brushes (long and short)
2. Brooms(long and short)
3. Duster
4. Soap
5. sponge
6. Detergent
7. Dust pan
8. Disinfectant, etc.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Asks pupils to state different parts of the home, note their points on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Sitting room, master and guest bedrooms, kitchen, store, etc.
Teacher’s remark - Celebrate the pupils for active responses. Display chart showing bathrooms and toilets for the pupils to identify and describe different types.
MEANING OF BATHROOM AND TOILET
A bathroom is a place in the home where we waste our body. That’s, a place where we take our bath.
A toilet is a place in the room where humans get rid of waste (urine and feces) that comes from their bodies.
In modern home, some houses are built with both bathroom and toilet as a single room while other are built separately.
TYPES OF TOILETS AND BATHROOMS
1. Pit latrine toilet
2. Bucket toilet
3. Water system
ASSIGNMENT
Find out the reason for cleaning the bathrooms and toilets.
LESSON 2 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Based on the assignment, display chart showing clean and unclean bathrooms and toilets for the pupils to state the difference.
Pupil’s Activities - This bathroom and toilet are cleaned but other are dirty.
Teacher’s remark - Correct. Good job you. Ask the pupils to state the reasons why we should keep out bathrooms and toilets clean. Note the points of discussion on the board.
REASONS FOR CLEANING TOILETS AND BATHROOMS
1. For easy usage.
2. To prevent accidents in the toilet or bathroom.
3. To prevent the floor from slippery.
4. To prevent germs, insects and diseases.
5. To prevent bad odour.
ASSIGNMENT
Find out the different materials used for cleaning the bathrooms and toilets.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Discuss reasons for cleaning toilets and bathrooms.
3. Finds out how many pupils clean toilets and bathrooms in their homes.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the class discussion.
4. Summary the points on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. mention types of toilet and bathrooms.
2. give three reasons for cleaning bathrooms and toilets.
WORKBOOK
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT (TEST)
1. A ___________ is a place where humans get rid of waste (urine and feces) that comes from their bodies.
A. Toilet/bathroom
B. Bathroom/bedroom
C. Toilet/bedroom
2. ___________ is a ceramic product that is used as a toilet and flushing the waste.
A. Latrine system
B. Bucket system
C. Water system
3. ___________ is kinds of toilet inside the house.
A. Latrine system
B. Bucket system
C. Water system
4. ___________ is kinds of toilet outside the house.
A. Latrine system
B. Toilet system
C. Water system
5. ___________ is the best and most hygiene toilet.
A. Water system
B. Bucket system
C. Latrine system
6. Unclean toilet and bathroom make the floor ___________.
A. better
B. Best
C. slippery
7. Unclean toilet and bathroom attract ___________.
A. good odour
B. bad odour
C. flies and germs
8. Clean toilet and bathroom ___________.
A. neat and tidy
B. neat and dirty
C. neat and better
9. Clean toilet and bathroom make ___________.
A. smile fine
B. smile bad
C. Smile better
10. The school toilet is ___________.
A. clean
B. dirty
C. unclean

Teacher’s Activities - Display chart showing a man/woman cleaning the bathroom and toilet for the children to identify and describe the activities on the chart.
Pupil’s Activities - The man/woman is cleaning the bathroom and toilet.
Teacher’s remark - Good job you. There are techniques used in cleaning bathrooms and toilets. Today, we will learn these techniques and apply them in our school’s toilets.
TOILET CLEANING TECHNIQUES
1. Flush the toilet after use.
2. Wash your hands after using the toilet.
3. Wash the toilet regularly.
4. Always close the door of the toilet.
BATHROOM CLEANING TECHNIQUES
1. Clean the bathroom mirror.
2. Don’t allow water log after bath.
3. Put your toothbrush in its position.
4. Sweep your bathroom.
PRACTICAL CLEANING OF SCHOOL TOILETS
Lead and guide the pupils to properly clean the toilets in the school.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Discuss the techniques used for cleaning the bathrooms and toilets.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate activities in the discussion.
3. Demonstrates how to clean toilets and bathrooms.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate in the cleaning process.
4. Finds out how many pupils clean toilets and bathrooms in their homes.
Pupil’s Activities - Clean toilet at home.
5. Summary the points on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. mention types of toilet and bathrooms.
2. give three reasons for cleaning bathrooms and toilets.
3. demonstrate two ways they will clean toilets and bathrooms in their homes.
4. state two reasons for taking good care of tools used in cleaning.
